{{Top|notoc=1}}
{{Quote|If these new droids do work out, I want to transmit my application to the Academy this year.''"<br />"''You mean the next semester before the harvest?''"<br />"''Sure, there's more than enough droids.''"<br />"''Harvest is when I need you the most. Only one more season. This year we'll make enough on the harvest so I'll be able to hire more hands. And then you can go to the Academy next year. You must understand I need you here, Luke.''"<br />"''But it's a whole 'nother year.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]]|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
A '''standard year''', also known more simply as a '''year''' or formally as '''Galactic Standard Year''',<ref name="GG2">''[[Galaxy Guide 2: Yavin and Bespin]]''</ref> was a standard measurement of [[Time/Legends|time]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The term '''year''' often referred to a single revolution of a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] around its [[Star/Legends|star]], the duration of which varied between planets; the standard year was specifically a [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] year, which was the galactic standard.<ref name="RPG2">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref><ref name="Revised">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> The Coruscant solar cycle was 368 days long with a day consisting of 24 standard hours.<ref name="wizards">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030403coruscant|text=Coruscant: Center of the Empire|int=Coruscant: Center of the Empire}}</ref>

The length of a [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] year was determined by the [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] radius and speed of the planet. Satellite planets&mdash;[[Moon/Legends|moons]] orbiting a [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]]&mdash;were almost always tide-locked to the gas giant they orbited, and may have had days several dozen hours long (as long as it took the satellite to orbit the gas giant). The local year of a satellite depended on the orbit of the gas giant and may have been several standard years long.<ref name="Planets of the Galaxy, Volume One">''[[Planets of the Galaxy, Volume One]]''</ref>

A standard year had been originally defined as 10 [[Standard month/Legends|standard months]] + 3 festival weeks + 3 holidays = 368 standard days,<ref name="RPG2" /><ref name="Revised" /> defining the [[Galactic Standard Calendar]].<ref name="LE">''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''</ref> However, [[Great ReSynchronization|calendar reforms]]<ref name="HNN 45">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|life/13228_2.html|RM&S; Debates Calendar Reform}}</ref> had eventually changed the Galactic Standard Calendar to a 12-month/368-day calendar.<ref name="MCBY">{{Blog|holocron|13/comments|Major Character Birth Years}}</ref><ref name="DRT">{{Blog|eeusuestornii|7|Don't Read This!!!!!!}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Although the standard year was originally defined as a 10-month year in the early [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]],<ref name="Revised" /> the keeper of the [[Holocron continuity database]] [[Leland Chee]] revealed in [[2005]] that the 10-month calendar system had been dropped for further publications and replaced by a more convenient 12-month calendar.<ref name="MCBY" /> The use of a 12-month/368-day calendar was later confirmed by [[Sue Rostoni]].<ref name="DRT" /> Thus, the reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' featured years of 12 months and months of 30 or 31 days.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

[[Karen Traviss]] had claimed that she used the 10-month calendar when writing her ''[[Republic Commando]]'' novels<ref name="SWBoards 1">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=222689&start=1230#13478643|thread=Books, Comics, & Television VIPs|user=[[Karen Traviss]]|date=2005-12-03|time=12:48 PM}}</ref><ref name="SWBoards 2">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=222689&start=1365#13853393|thread=Books, Comics, & Television VIPs|user=[[Karen Traviss]]|date=2006-01-16|time=2:00 AM}}</ref>&mdash;despite the fact that, in said novels, the one-year anniversary of the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]] occurs approximately twelve months after the battle.<ref name="AnniversaryDates">Karen Traviss's novel ''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]'' dates the [[Battle of Qiilura]] to three months after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]]. Furthermore, the events of the main section of ''Republic Commando: Triple Zero'', which take place nine months after the Battle of Qiilura, span twenty-eight days and begin on the [[Standard day/Legends|day]] before the one-[[Standard year/Legends|year]] anniversary of the First Battle of Geonosis. Therefore the one-year anniversary of the First Battle of Geonosis must have taken place twelve months after the battle.</ref>
